description:
## CONTEXT

Text-only hardening of the eight lens prompts and the shared preamble. No schema changes; independent of LF1-LF4, so it can ship in parallel. From the 2026-07-03 prompts review (decision record: workspace N-076). The static prompts are distilled review-vector specs (owner floor+edge ruling): hardening them raises the floor that every execution tier inherits, so review quality does not depend on a strong reviewer being present at run time.

## VERIFIED STATE @ a9f49dd

- No lens prompt requires a refutation pass before reporting. A grep for `refute`/`disprove`/"before reporting" over src/lenses/prompts returns nothing. Tools are Read/Grep/Glob read-only (shared-preamble.ts:149-155). Only security and concurrency approach active verification (security.ts:109,145; concurrency.ts:31); test-quality is pure pattern inspection.
- Checklists are JS/TS/React/Swift-centric with no language-adaptation instruction: error-handling references `.catch()`, `Promise.all`/`allSettled`, and `tsconfig.json` strict mode (error-handling.ts:28,30,31,45,55); performance references `fs.readFileSync`/`execSync`/`useMemo` (performance.ts:83,85); concurrency embeds Swift actor isolation and Node/Express module-state (concurrency.ts:34,35). Performance activates on `.py`/`.go`/`.rs`/`.java` (registry.ts:135-155), so it reviews Python with JS idioms.
- Confidence floor is inconsistent: only security.ts:167 and concurrency.ts:80 state "Below 0.6: Do NOT report." The other six lenses lack a hard floor. Shared preamble rule 7 (shared-preamble.ts:100) has a self-granted escape hatch ("unless you have strong corroborating evidence from tool use").
- test-quality (test-quality.ts:44-57) has "Test data coupling" (line 55) but no fixture-provenance item and no "would this test fail if the implementation were broken" (mutation-style) item.
- `ticketDescription` is rendered into context (shared-preamble.ts:159-163) but no lens is told to check the diff against the ticket's stated intent.
- No data-safety/migrations lens exists: clean-code explicitly ignores "Generated code, migration files, lock files" (clean-code.ts:46) and no other lens claims destructive DDL, backfills, or missing tenant/RLS scoping (SURFACE_RULES, registry.ts:130-186).
- `findingBudget` is fixed at 10 (prompt-builder.ts:27) with no diff-size depth scaling. PLAN_REVIEW activates all lenses unconditionally (registry.ts:317-318).

## SCOPE (text-only edits to shared-preamble.ts, the eight prompt bodies, one new prompt body + its surface rule)

1. Shared "Before reporting: attempt to refute" block in the preamble: (a) read the full enclosing function/file, not just the hunk; (b) actively Grep for guards/middleware/callers that neutralize the finding; (c) report only if the refutation attempt fails, recording what you checked in `description`.
2. Language-adaptation sentence in the preamble (or each "What to review" preface): "Checklist examples use JS/TS idioms for concreteness; translate each pattern to the reviewed language's equivalents (e.g. Python bare except / asyncio.gather / requests without timeout; Go ignored err returns; SQL missing parameterization)."
3. Uniform hard confidence floor: append the "Below {floor}: Do NOT report." line to all eight confidence guides (currently only security.ts:167 and concurrency.ts:80 have it); tighten preamble rule 7 (shared-preamble.ts:100) to define "strong corroborating evidence" as "a specific Read/Grep observation you cite in `description`."
4. test-quality additions (test-quality.ts): "Fixture provenance -- fixtures that fabricate data violating domain invariants or hand-copied from implementation output rather than derived from the schema or real samples"; and a CODE_REVIEW checklist item "For each test, name the implementation bug it would catch; flag tests for which no such bug exists."
5. Spec-conformance instruction in the preamble: "If a ticket description is present, verify the change actually implements it; report divergence as category `spec-conformance`."
6. New `data-safety` surface-activated lens: add a surface rule on `migrations/`, `*.sql`, and schema files (registry.ts SURFACE_RULES, registry.ts:130-186) and register the body in `LENSES`. Covers destructive DDL, backfill ordering, missing tenant/RLS scoping on new queries, and irreversible writes. Set `maxSeverity` per policy (major or critical); wire canonical categories if it should feed blocking policy.
7. Diff-size depth scaling line in the preamble: "If the diff exceeds ~15 files or ~1000 changed lines, prioritize files matching your lens surface and state in notes which files you did not examine; for small diffs (<100 lines), verify every checklist item exhaustively."
8. PLAN_REVIEW plan-kind hint: let the caller pass a plan-kind (`ui`/`backend`/`infra`) that filters obviously inapplicable lenses before spawn (the unconditional all-lenses branch is registry.ts:317-318). Minimal form: the hint rides `lensConfig` and `activate()` honors it.

## OUT OF SCOPE

Schema changes (LF1/LF3/LF4); the full content-aware selection engine and project-local custom lenses (LF7 -- item 8 here is only the coarse plan-kind hint, not a DiffProfile).

## ACCEPTANCE

- Pinned preamble tests (test/shared-preamble.test.ts) assert the refute block, the language-adaptation sentence, the spec-conformance sentence, and the depth-scaling line appear verbatim.
- The lens-bodies structural test asserts all eight confidence guides contain the hard-floor line.
- The test-quality body contains the fixture-provenance and mutation-style items.
- The new `data-safety` lens is registered, activates on a `*.sql` changed file, and stays inert on a pure UI diff; a lens-registry-activate test pins both.
- The V1 denylist test (test/lens-bodies.test.ts:97-106) still passes -- no new body mentions a banned token; refer to a "quoted Read/Grep observation", never `evidence` or `suggestedFix`.
- PLAN_REVIEW with a plan-kind of `backend` does not activate accessibility.

## PITFALLS

- Do NOT introduce the tokens `evidence` or `suggestedFix` into any lens body (test/lens-bodies.test.ts:97-106); phrase the refutation and floor language without them.
- The new lens must not create a demarcation gap with clean-code -- give `data-safety` the destructive-DDL lane and keep clean-code's ignore bullet (clean-code.ts:46).
- Depth-scaling text governs prioritization, not the `findingBudget` number; do not contradict the fixed budget.
- Keep every prompt model-agnostic -- the codebase already enforces no model names in bodies; do not regress it.

## VERIFICATION

Render each lens body for both stages and diff against updated pinned snapshots; run an activation fixture that adds a migration file and asserts `data-safety` fires while accessibility stays off; spot-check that a Python-diff render now carries the language-adaptation sentence.

## SIZING

M. All text; the only structural piece is registering one new lens plus its surface rule. Portable enough for the lowest permitted execution tier because each edit is a localized prompt change with a pinned assertion.

Cross-link: workspace N-076. Independent of LF1-LF4.
title: Prompt floor hardening -- refutation pass, language adaptation, uniform confidence floor, fixture provenance, spec conformance, data-safety lens
